'''Stephen James Blyth''' (born September 1967)<ref>{{cite web |title=Stephen James BLYTH |url=https://find-and-update.company-information.service.gov.uk/officers/R5cAsZd-DbjlUKhe05ec2kWmJVA/appointments |access-date=26 September 2025}}</ref> is a British mathematician and academic. From October 2022 to September 2025 he was [[List of principals of Lady Margaret Hall, Oxford|Principal]] of [[Lady Margaret Hall, Oxford]].<ref name="takes up">{{cite web |title=Professor Stephen Blyth takes up Principalship of LMH |url=https://www.lmh.ox.ac.uk/news/professor-stephen-blyth-takes-principalship-lmh |website=Lady Margaret Hall |publisher=University of Oxford |access-date=18 February 2023 |language=en}}</ref> He had been Professor of the Practice of Statistics at [[Harvard University]] since 2012,<ref name="elected">{{cite web |title=Prof Stephen Blyth elected to be next Principal of LMH |url=https://www.lmh.ox.ac.uk/news/professor-stephen-blyth-elected-next-principal |website=Lady Margaret Hall |publisher=University of Oxford |access-date=18 February 2023 |language=en}}</ref><ref name="Statistics">{{cite web |last1=Shephard |first1=Neil |title=Professor Stephen Blyth appointed Principal of Lady Margaret Hall, Oxford |url=https://statistics.fas.harvard.edu/news/professor-stephen-blyth-appointed-principal-lady-margaret-hall-oxford |website=Department of Statistics |publisher=Harvard University |access-date=18 February 2023 |language=en |date=13 December 2021}}</ref> and was also chief executive officer of the [[Harvard Management Company]] between January 2015 and July 2016.<ref name="THG">{{cite news |last1=Mitchell |first1=Stephanie |title=Stephen Blyth to lead Harvard Management Company |url=https://news.harvard.edu/gazette/story/2014/09/stephen-blyth-to-lead-harvard-management-company/ |access-date=18 February 2023 |work=[[The Harvard Gazette]] |date=24 September 2014}}</ref><ref name="Resigns">{{cite news |last1=Rosenberg |first1=John S. |title=Stephen Blyth Resigns from Harvard Management Company |url=https://www.harvardmagazine.com/2016/07/harvard-endowment-ceo-stephen-blyth-resigns |access-date=18 February 2023 |work=[[Harvard Magazine]] |date=27 July 2016 |language=en}}</ref>

==Biography==
Blyth [[matriculated]] into [[Christ's College, Cambridge]], in 1985 to study the [[Mathematical Tripos]].<ref name="Christ's">{{cite web |title=Professor Stephen Blyth elected next Principal of LMH |url=https://www.christs.cam.ac.uk/news/professor-stephen-blyth-elected-next-principal-lmh |website=Christ's College |publisher=University of Cambridge |access-date=18 February 2023 |date=19 December 2021}}</ref> He graduated with a [[first class honours]] Bachelor of Arts (BA) degree,<ref name="Christ's" /> and was the 3rd [[Wrangler (University of Cambridge)|wrangler]] in that year.<ref name="takes up" /> He then moved to the United States, where he studied statistics at [[Harvard University]].<ref name="Statistics" /> He was awarded a Master of Arts (AM) degree in 1989.<ref name="bio stats">{{cite web |title=Stephen Blyth Professor of the Practice in Statistics |url=https://statistics.fas.harvard.edu/people/stephen-blyth |website=Department of Statistics |publisher=Harvard University |access-date=18 February 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211202104049/https://statistics.fas.harvard.edu/people/stephen-blyth |archive-date=2 December 2021}}</ref> His [[doctoral dissertation]] was titled "Local Regression Coefficients and the Correlation Curve" and his advisor was Kjell Doksum.<ref name="Genealogy">{{cite web |title=Stephen Blyth |url=https://www.genealogy.math.ndsu.nodak.edu/id.php?id=61469 |website=The Mathematics Genealogy Project |access-date=18 February 2023}}</ref> His Doctor of Philosophy (PhD) degree was awarded in 1992.<ref name="Genealogy" />

After graduating with his PhD, he returned to England and was a lecturer in the Department of Mathematics at [[Imperial College London]] from 1992 to 1994.<ref name="THG" /><ref name="bio stats" /> He then moved into the [[financial industry]], working at [[HSBC]], [[Morgan Stanley]] and [[Deutsche Bank]].<ref name="elected" /><ref name="bio stats" /> In 2006, he returned to Harvard University where he joined the [[Academic personnel|faculty]].<ref name="Statistics" /> He taught statistics in the [[Harvard Faculty of Arts and Sciences]],<ref name="THG" /> rising to become Professor of the Practice of Statistics in 2012.<ref name="Statistics" /> He also worked with the [[Harvard Management Company]] (HMC) which manages Harvard University's endowment and related financial assets.<ref name="THG" /> By 2014, he was managing director and head of public markets.<ref name="THG" /> In September 2014, he was announced as the next president and chief executive officer of the Harvard Management Company:<ref name="THG" /> he took up the post on 1 January 2015.<ref name="Leave">{{cite news |title=Harvard Management Company Leader Takes Medical Leave |url=https://www.harvardmagazine.com/2016/05/harvard-endowment-ceo-on-medical-leave |access-date=18 February 2023 |work=Harvard Magazine |date=23 May 2016 |language=en}}</ref> He took medical leave from 23 May 2016,<ref name="Resigns" /> and stepped down as CEO on 27 July 2016.<ref name="Resigns" />

In December 2021, Blyth was announced as the next [[Master (college)|Principal]] of [[Lady Margaret Hall, Oxford]].<ref name="elected" /><ref name="Christ's" /> He took up the post on 1 October 2022 and was installed during a service in the College Chapel on 7 October 2022.<ref name="takes up" />

In September 2025 it was announced that he would in Autumn 2025 join the [[Financial Policy Committee]] of the Bank of England, to serve a three year term.<ref>{{cite web| title=Stephen Blyth appointed, and Randall Kroszner reappointed to the Bank of England's Financial Policy Committee |url = https://www.gov.uk/government/news/stephen-blyth-appointed-and-randall-kroszner-reappointed-to-the-bank-of-englands-financial-policy-committee|website = HM Treasury}}</ref> On 23 October the [[Treasury Select Committee|Treasury Committee of the House of Commons]] approved his appointment.<ref>{{cite web |title=Appointment of Professor Stephen Blyth to the Financial Policy Committee |url=https://publications.parliament.uk/pa/cm5901/cmselect/cmtreasy/1396/report.html |access-date=25 October 2025}}</ref>
